caption_used: Coverage as a function of the number of completions (k) for Llama-3B, Llama-3B + FT, Llama-1B, and Llama-1B + FT. All four models exhibit monotonically increasing coverage with additional completions on a logarithmic x-axis from 2^0 to 2^8. The 3B models begin at approximately 0.42 coverage and reach roughly 0.92 at k=256, while the 1B variants start near 0.22 and plateau at approximately 0.72 by k=128 with minimal further gains. Notably, fine-tuning provides a consistent advantage of approximately 5 percentage points for the 1B model throughout the scaling curve, whereas the 3B base and fine-tuned variants remain largely indistinguishable.
raw_response: DESCRIPTION: The figure is a single line chart illustrating how coverage changes with the number of completions for four model variants. The x-axis is labeled “Number of completions (k)” and uses a logarithmic base-2 scale with tick labels from \(2^0\) through \(2^8\) (i.e., 1 to 256). The y-axis is labeled “Coverage” on a linear scale, spanning roughly from about 0.2 up to just under 1.0, with visible gridlines at regular intervals. There are four data series shown in the legend: “Llama-3B” is a blue solid line with circular markers that increases monotonically from about 0.42 at \(2^0\) to about 0.92 at \(2^8\); “Llama-3B + FT” is a green dotted line with triangular markers that closely tracks the blue series, rising from about 0.43 at \(2^0\) to about 0.92 at \(2^8\). “Llama-1B” is a light-blue solid line with circular markers that increases from about 0.22 at \(2^0\) to about 0.86 at \(2^8\), with intermediate points around ~0.55 at \(2^3\) and ~0.79 at \(2^6\). “Llama-1B + FT” is a light-green dotted line with triangular markers that follows a similar monotonic rise, starting near ~0.25 at \(2^0\) and ending near ~0.88 at \(2^8\), with values around ~0.60 at \(2^3\) and ~0.82 at \(2^6\). All four lines show steadily increasing coverage as \(k\) increases, with the two 3B curves nearly overlapping across the full x-range and the two 1B curves running close together with the fine-tuned variant slightly higher at most ticks.
